items.title: A Savannah police officer gave her Flock login to her ICE agent husband
items.summary: Now, former Savannah police officer Amber Harpe was fired in August following a department investigation that found she had shared her Flock login information with her husband, Tyler Harpe, an ICE agent. SPD does not share its Flock data with ICE and said sharing access to the sy
items.content:
SPD officer Amber Harpe was fired for sharing her Flock access with her ICE agent husband.

Now, former Savannah police officer Amber Harpe was fired in August following a department investigation that found she had shared her Flock login information with her husband, Tyler Harpe, an ICE agent. SPD does not share its Flock data with ICE and said sharing access to the system violated the department’s security protocols.

While he had unauthorized access to the system, Tyler Harpe conducted 983 searches related to 97 license plates, which were overwhelmingly registered to Hispanic drivers, according to Savannah’s local ABC affiliate, WJCL . The Harpes defended their actions, saying they didn’t use access for personal reasons and that the searches were strictly for “law-enforcement purposes.”

Interim Major Max Nowinsky originally recommended a light eight-hour suspension for Harpe. However, Major Michelle Halford and Assistant Police Chief Robert Gavin disagreed, and they removed her from the force. Harpe was fired, along with five other SPD employees, after an internal investigation uncovered Flock misuse. Four of them were later arrested; however, Harpe was not one of them.

items.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
items.summary: Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund.
items.content:
Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.

Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”

There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study . But the company said, “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”

Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”

If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.

items.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
items.summary: Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia's ABC13 "I know they're taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whe
items.content:
Carolyn Marvin was charged with ‘disorderly conduct’ for protesting delivery robots taking jobs.

Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia’s ABC13 “I know they’re taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front of them and preventing them from going forward.”

Police responded to the scene and asked Marvin to move out of the robot’s way. When she refused, they placed her in cuffs and arrested her. The incident was captured on video and has now garnered considerable media attention.

The delivery robots have become a common sight on the streets of downtown Philadelphia and have sparked backlash. This is not even Marvin’s first brush with them. And earlier this year, one was kicked over in Center City. Broad concern has grown about how autonomous systems, including robotaxis, delivery robots, and AI agents, are impacting jobs, especially for lower-skill workers .

items.title: Someone behind the software
items.summary: Article URL: https://karrisaarinen.com/posts/someone-behind-the-software/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50142573 Points: 270 # Comments: 112
items.content:
I think good products carry something of the people who make them. Their experience, what they care about, and how they think things should work. You might not know who those people are, but you can feel their perspective in the product.

The industry often talks about software as though it comes out of a factory. You collect requirements, build features, and measure whether they work. Follow the process and you should get a good result. Now we're talking automating this whole pipeline with agents.

But two teams can talk to similar customers, have access to the same technology, and make very different things. The difference comes from how they understand what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA also shapes this a lot.

At Linear , we have always valued intuition over process or data. I think people sometimes understand that as making decisions based on personal preference, without much thought or evidence. What we mean by it is that your intuition develops through experience and understanding. You work on something, talk to customers, make mistakes, and learn what to pay attention to. The intuition is your point of view on something, and forcing to use your judgment, not hide behind faceless data.

Before we launched, we talked to people across companies and roles about how they worked. We had our own frustrations with this type software, but those conversations helped us understand what mattered beyond our own experience. Our perspective got better after those conversations.

So eventually the products develops a character through what its makers pay attention to, what they decide not to do and what they keep working on after it technically works. I sometimes think of this as the soul of a product. You feel that someone cares about how the whole thing comes together.

A feature can work perfectly well on its own and still make the product worse. Recognizing that requires some belief about what the product should be. Someone has to make the call, then stay close enough to customers to see whether they were right.

Recently, many products are starting to feel messy to me, including products from very successful companies. There seems to be more thought going into what the technology can do and what can be added than the form it should take. The product changes are primarily additive, not improving the core problem.

I think the reasons for this is that it's lot easier to add new capabilities, than rethink existing capabilities. So each product becomes a collection of abilities, without actually having unified point of view.

I wonder whether some of this comes from how the work is organized. Individuals work with agents to produce changes independently, each operating a small software factory. Each change might make sense on its own, but together they start to resemble Frankenstein’s monster rather than a carefully shaped sculpture.

Without the shared perspective, soul, or thought, the product becomes an average of all those outputs. The choices that once gave it character are being diluted by day. More things work, but it becomes harder to feel someone or even something behind them.

Making software is getting easier. I hope that gives people more room to develop a perspective and follow it further. To understand a problem deeply and keep shaping an answer until the pieces belong together.

I want to feel the creator behind the software, not the factories.

items.title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
items.summary: The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer.
items.content:
After chatbot startup Character.AI filed for bankruptcy earlier this week, many of its employees will have the opportunity to take jobs at Disney.

Character.AI’s former CEO Karandeep Anand recently became the entertainment giant’s first CTO , and the startup previously said that Disney had agreed to acquire some of its assets for $20 million.

A legal filing spotted by Bloomberg revealed more details about the agreement between Character.AI and Disney, with Disney agreeing to make employment offers to at least 60 Character.AI employees — the majority of the workforce — paying them an estimated $60 million in annual compensation.

The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer.

The filing says that despite its “large and engaged user base,” Character.AI has been hobbled by high costs and “potential litigation-related liabilities and regulatory engagement.” (The company was sued by the mother of a 14-year-old boy who said her son became obsessed with one of Character.AI’s chatbots before committing suicide; it also faces government investigations over child safety concerns .)

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: The outside watchdog can publish its findings without Anthropic's approval.
items.content:
Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control.

METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems.

A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large.

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei achieved a rare moment of unity with arch-rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk in September when the OpenAI and SpaceX bosses rallied behind his proposal to embed external auditors in the leading labs.

Thursday’s announcement marks the first step to implementing these pledges. OpenAI has yet to lay out plans to bring in evaluators after Altman said Amodei’s proposals were a good idea.

“As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessment,” Anthropic said on Thursday. “We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work.”

Critics of Anthropic’s proposal to use evaluators have argued the arrangements could lead to conflicts of interest, pointing to issues in the accounting sector, and that greater government regulation is required.

Anthropic argued that sharing information publicly could benefit malicious actors or competitors and added that its evaluators will operate similarly to bank supervision, whereby regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks.

“If a bank’s risk-taking could threaten the public, third parties try to see that in advance,” the company said.

Anthropic is also under pressure to reassure investors that safety issues will not overshadow its initial public offering, expected this year at a more than $2tn valuation. It devoted a large part of investor presentations this week to laying out its safety practices.

METR was one of the organisations that investigated the hack of Hugging Face by rogue OpenAI models, reviewing thousands of logs and receiving company laptops.

Anthropic has now onboarded six METR employees, giving them company hardware, office space and “access to internal tools and systems that are roughly on par with what our own risk assessment teams have access to.”

The lab said it has encouraged employees to share information with the evaluators as they would with a fellow employee working in risk.

Anthropic is not paying METR for this arrangement. The research group does not accept donations from AI companies or their staff. It is funded by donations from individuals and philanthropic organisations, as well as government bodies such as the UK’s AI Security Institute.

The evaluators will publish their analysis, and Anthropic cannot veto publication. However, it can require them to redact information that falls into certain categories, such as customer data, details covered by attorney-client privilege or information about model architectures.

Anthropic added it was still working with Accenture, which was named a partner on safety testing last month, with each committing at least $1 billion to set up new safeguards.

Another third-party tester is SecureBio, which reviews chemical and biological weapon risk for the company.

“We’re embedding evaluators voluntarily, and we believe every frontier AI company should do the same,” Anthropic said.

METR said: “We stand ready to work with all frontier AI developers to bring better evidence to the public.”

items.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Rivian’s next act
items.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
items.content:
As I wrapped my TechCrunch Disrupt interview with Rivian CEO and founder RJ Scaringe , I kept circling back to one question: What does Scaringe want Rivian to become? If you look at Rivian’s moves over the past year, it’s clear that Scaringe wants the company to be much more than an EV maker. But he doesn’t want to stray completely from that mission either.

Rivian is far more vertically integrated than it was just a couple of years ago. It has developed its own AI models to power its in-vehicle assistant and is building an end-to-end automated driving stack for its passenger vehicles and future robotaxis through a partnership with Uber. It’s even developing custom silicon , a 5 nm processor in collaboration with Arm and TSMC. And then there is its $5.8 billion joint technology venture with VW Group focused on electric architecture and software.

Scaringe’s ambitions extend beyond Rivian as well, although there is always a link back. He created a micromobility skunkworks program that has since spun out into a startup called Also. And he founded an industrial robotics startup called Mind Robotics, which is now 31% owned by Rivian and counts the automaker as a prospective customer. (Scaringe announced onstage that former Ford, Apple, and Tesla executive Doug Field has been hired as president of Mind Robotics.)

Scaringe’s aspirations were on display as he talked of not only expanding the joint venture with VW to cover AI and autonomy, but also licensing Rivian’s tech to “many different brands.”

So what does Rivian look like at the end of the decade? Certainly not just a maker of electric trucks and SUVs. The term I kept coming back to was “tech supplier.”

Hear me out. Rivian is clearing a path toward licensing its electric architecture and software as well as its AI models and autonomy stack. Meanwhile, the Mind Robotics startup it partially owns is building industrial robots to not only be used in Rivian factories, but also sold to other companies. Then there’s the robotaxi business. A successful launch with Uber could open the door to more deals.

And Scaringe is already imagining how autonomy could reshape Rivian’s own vehicles.

“Where it gets really interesting is then you think beyond R2 and R3 and start to imagine the form factors that you want to build for a personally owned autonomous vehicle. You know, it opens up all kinds of design opportunities. It can create dramatically different experiences,” he said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I’m wildly excited about what the next 10 years look like in transportation because of what this enables us to dream and think about.”

Bedrock Robotics , a startup developing autonomous driving tech for construction vehicles, is raising $600 million , Axios reported, citing sources.

Dot Ai completed its acquisition of electric vehicle car-sharing business Envoy Technologies in a $65 million all-stock transaction, according to a regulatory filing .

Evos , a startup that developed AI agents to automate work for industrial businesses, including freight brokerages, raised $9 million in a pre-seed round co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures.

Mana Battery, a Colorado-based startup developing anode-free sodium batteries, raised $10.15 million in a round led by Voyager Ventures.

PlusAI , the autonomous trucking developer, and Texas Ventures Acquisition III filed a Form S-4 registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission —advancing its previously announced agreement to go public via a merger with a blank-check company.

Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia. Neither company shared financial terms of the deal. The automaker plans to use a trio of Nvidia products to be able to offer hands-free, point-to-point driving on highways and surface streets.

Waabi , a startup developing self-driving trucks, landed a commercial partnership with carrier Warrior Logistics. Under the deal, Waabi’s self-driving trucks will move freight between Dallas and Houston.

Electric vehicle sales in the United States are showing signs of life .

Laplace Intelligence , one of 20 startups that competed in TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200, is building automated red-teaming that stress-tests robots and self-driving cars.

MIT startup LNK Energies says it has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen , slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from price spikes.

The Paris Auto Show puts Chinese cars on center stage.

Tesla showcased its SpaceX-powered Roadster with a theatrical kickflip stunt. The Roadster used a mix of high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin around, and stick a landing on the pavement below. CEO Elon Musk claims the vehicle will be on the road by 2028. But will future owners be allowed to legally deploy these maneuvers on public streets? I don’t see how.

Waymo is expanding into Canada — specifically, Toronto — after receiving approval to participate in an automated vehicle pilot program. Waymo has also opened up its robotaxi service to everyone, meaning no more waitlists, in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa.

TechCrunch reporter Tim De Chant recently test drove the 2026Porsche Macan Turbo EV . His week with the EV has him questioning what a sports car is supposed to be. Read the full review.

items.content:

압둘아지즈 빈 탈랄(Abdulaziz bin Talal) 왕자, AGFUND 소액금융은행 설립자들이 개발 성과의 토대를 마련했다고 평가

방콕 , 2026년 10월 18일 /PRNewswire/ -- 아랍걸프개발프로그램(Arab Gulf Programme for Development, AGFUND)이 세계저축은행협회(World Savings and Retail Banking Institute, WSBI)가 유럽저축은행협회(European Savings and Retail Banking Group, ESBG)와 공동으로 주최한 2026 지속가능발전목표 시상식(2026 Sustainable Development Goals Awards)에서 '포용금융 및 사회적 영향 부문 우수상(Excellence in Inclusive Banking and Social Impact)'을 수상했다.

AGFUND CEO Hammam bin Nasser bin Juraid receives the “Excellence in Inclusive Banking and Social Impact” award at the 2026 WSBI–ESBG Sustainable Development Goals Awards in Bangkok, Thailand, on 16 October 2026

AGFUND의 함맘 빈 나세르 빈 주라이드(Hammam bin Nasser bin Juraid) 최고경영자가 국제통화기금(International Monetary Fund)과 세계은행그룹(World Bank Group) 연차총회 기간에 태국 방콕에서 이 상을 받았다.

AGFUND 총재인 압둘아지즈 빈 탈랄 빈 압둘아지즈 왕자는 이번 수상이 금융서비스를 활용해 소외된 지역사회의 역량을 강화하고 생계를 개선하며 경제적 자립을 촉진해 온 AGFUND의 경험을 인정한 것이라고 밝혔다.

그는 사람들의 역량 강화에 중점을 둔 기관을 설립한 AGFUND 소액금융은행 설립자들, 특히 고(故) 탈랄 빈 압둘아지즈(Talal bin Abdulaziz) 왕자의 공로를 높이 평가했다.

이어 이번 수상에는 20년 넘게 이어온 헌신과 포용적 금융 은행 및 협력기관의 노력, 지원받은 자금으로 사업을 일구고 가계 소득을 창출한 고객들의 노력이 반영되어 있다고 덧붙였다. 또한 기회를 확대하고 사람들의 삶에 지속적인 개선을 가져왔는지를 기준으로 성공을 평가해야 한다고 강조했다.

압둘아지즈 왕자는 이번 수상이 소외 계층에 서비스를 제공하는 기관의 가치를 보여주며, 각 가정의 금융 접근성과 경제적 기회 확대를 장려한다고 강조했다.

AGFUND의 포용적 금융 은행 네트워크는 출범 이후 130만 명이 넘는 고객에게 서비스를 제공하고 미화 13억 7000만 달러 이상의 자금을 지원했다. 여성이 대출 고객의 59%를 차지한다는 점은 이 네트워크가 경제적 역량 강화에 기여하고 있음을 보여준다.

1924년 설립된 WSBI가 ESBG와 함께 수여하는 이 상은 금융서비스와 사회적 영향, 지속 가능한 발전을 연계하는 접근법을 인정한다.

AGFUND는 2004년 요르단에 첫 번째 은행을 설립한 이후 요르단, 예멘, 바레인, 시리아, 레바논, 팔레스타인, 수단, 모리타니, 시에라리온 등 9개국으로 사업을 확대했으며, 기존 금융기관의 서비스를 충분히 이용하지 못하는 지역사회에 주력해 왔다.

이 네트워크는 150만 건 이상의 대출을 실행하고 92만 7000개 이상의 저축 계좌를 개설했으며, 112개 지점을 설립하고 1500명 이상을 고용했다. 영세 및 소기업과 소득 창출 활동에 자금을 지원하는 서비스를 통해 생계 개선과 경제적 자립을 돕고 있다.

AGFUND는 개발 협력을 강화하고 디지털 솔루션과 혁신적인 금융상품을 발전시키는 한편, 자금 지원을 교육, 역량 개발, 시장 접근, 위험 대비와 연계할 계획이다.

또한 성공적인 접근법을 현지 수요에 맞게 적용하는 기관 간 협력을 통해 특히 아프리카를 중심으로 사업 지역 확대를 모색하고, 더 많은 지역사회에 지속 가능한 포용금융을 제공하고자 한다.

글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/10/19 00:10

광저우, 중국 2026년 10월 18일 /PRNewswire/ -- 지난 10월 15일 캔톤 페어(Canton Fair) 전시장에서 캔톤 페어 바이어 연합(Canton Fair Buyers Alliance)이 공식 출범하면서 창설 70주년을 맞은 캔톤 페어의 중요한 이정표가 됐다.

출범식에는 140여 명의 해외 바이어가 참석해 글로벌 상거래와 중국 수출 부문을 연결하는 가교로서 캔톤 페어가 꾸준히 수행해 온 역할을 부각했다.

이날 출범식에서 조인코(Joinco, Import & Export, Ltd.)의 루이스 빌라리사(Luís Vilariça) 최고경영자(CEO)는 자사와 캔톤 페어의 오랜 인연을 소개했다. 그는 다년간의 참가 경험을 바탕으로 중국 공급업체와의 협력을 통해 창출된 성장 기회를 돌아보고, 국제 사업 개발과 글로벌 무역 교류를 지원하는 캔톤 페어의 역할을 강조했다.

출범식에서는 연합 회원사들의 공동 선언도 발표됐다. 5개 회원사 대표가 각자의 모국어로 선언문을 낭독하며 새로 출범한 조직의 국제적 성격을 강조했다. 다른 회원사들도 축하 영상을 보내 출범을 함께 축하하고 연합의 공식 출범을 지켜봤다.

캔톤 페어 바이어 연합은 캔톤 페어의 핵심 서비스 혁신 사례 중 하나다. 주로 포춘 글로벌 500대(Fortune Global 500) 기업, 세계 250대 유통업체의 바이어, 다양한 시장의 선도적인 소싱 기업을 대상으로 설계된 이 연합은 회원사에 정보 공유와 자원 조율을 위한 플랫폼을 제공하는 것을 목표로 한다. 첫 회원사로는 5개 대륙 32개 국가 및 지역의 58개 기업이 참여했다. 회원사들은 연합을 통해 서비스, 행사, 자원, 정보 등 4대 영역에 걸쳐 다양한 우대 혜택을 누릴 수 있다.

items.content:
With double the RAM and storage of the base Steam Deck OLED, plus a slightly faster processor, this is a great deal.

The Legion Go S with SteamOS is a pretty solid alternative to the $789 Steam Deck OLED. It runs identical software, but ships in a design with two-stage triggers, a bigger eight-inch IPS screen (1080p and up to 120Hz versus 800p and 90Hz in the Deck OLED), and it’s got double the RAM and storage (32GB and 1TB, respectively), not to mention a slightly faster processor in the Ryzen Z1 Extreme.

At $999.99, its current discounted price at Best Buy , it’s worth considering if you’re deciding on a handheld. The Legion Go S is not as powerful as the $1,299.99 Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 that just launched, which has the Z2 Extreme and a OLED screen, but it’s no slouch, either.

This model launched with Windows 11 and the Ryzen Z2 Go. Despite being a newer chip, it’s less powerful than the Z1 Extreme in the discounted model. SteamOS and the faster internals within this configuration will provide a better experience. Check out my colleague Sean Hollister’s review of multiple configs of the Go S, and see how it stacks up in his benchmarks.
